bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices — this guide follows the Ruger Mark IV push-button take-down as documented in Ruger’s own Mark IV manual, which Volquartsen’s own page says the Volquartsen Mamba-TF shares. It is not Volquartsen’s manual for this model. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never take this firearm further apart than this guide goes.
cleanIntro:
No manual from Volquartsen exists for this model, but Volquartsen’s own page says the Volquartsen Mamba-TF is built on the Ruger Mark IV frame with its push-button take-down, and that take-down is documented by Ruger’s own Mark IV manual. This guide follows it: clear, one button, two assemblies, the bolt out — and nothing further.

Listed in Fieldstrip as .22 LR. The chambering marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose cartridge, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Confirm yours is built the Mark IV way
steps.action: Look for the pattern: a round take-down button at the rear of the frame, just below the bolt, and a bolt that cocks by a pair of ears at the back of the receiver. That button is this whole guide.
steps.prose: ⛔ No button there, or a different upper than your maker’s page shows? Stop: clean the pistol with the bolt held open and put the question to Volquartsen.

steps.title: Magazine out, bolt back, look and feel — twice
steps.action: Remove the magazine first. Draw the bolt fully rearward by its ears and look into the chamber, then touch it with a fingertip — on a .22 the case rim hides easily. Ease the bolt forward, then check the same way a second time.
steps.quote: Draw the bolt fully rearward and visually inspect the chamber to be certain that there is no cartridge in it and then release the bolt.
steps.cite: Ruger Mark IV Instruction Manual — PM1179 — Disassembly, step 1, p.21
steps.warn: Always unload a firearm before cleaning, lubrication, disassembly, or assembly.

steps.title: Press the take-down button
steps.action: Hold the barrel in one hand and the grip frame in the other, and press the take-down button at the rear of the frame, just below the bolt.
steps.quote: Holding the barrel in one hand and the grip frame assembly in the other, depress the take-down button located just below the rear of the bolt
steps.cite: Ruger Mark IV Instruction Manual — PM1179 — Disassembly, step 2, p.21

steps.title: Barrel tilted down, upper lifted off
steps.action: With the button pressed, tilt the barrel downward until it clears the bolt stop pin, then lift the barrel/receiver assembly straight up off the grip frame.
steps.quote: The barrel/receiver assembly can now be lifted straight up off of the grip frame assembly
steps.cite: Ruger Mark IV Instruction Manual — PM1179 — Disassembly, step 3, p.21

steps.title: Bolt out by its ears — and that is the end of it
steps.action: Pull straight back on the bolt ears and draw the bolt out of the receiver. Ruger’s own line closes the strip: nothing else comes off, and everything in the grip frame is Volquartsen’s work.
steps.quote: Pull straight back on the bolt ears to remove the bolt from the receiver
steps.cite: Ruger Mark IV Instruction Manual — PM1179 — Disassembly, step 5, p.21

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, bolt face wiped
steps.action: With the upper off, brush the bore wet with solvent from the chamber end, then dry patches until clean and a lightly oiled patch for storage — .22 rimfire fouling is waxy and comes off the chamber mouth with a nylon brush. Wipe the bolt face and the receiver’s bolt raceway; a thin film of oil on the bolt’s bearing surfaces, and none into the firing-pin channel.

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the receiver, the barrel and the grip frame for cracks, the bolt face for a peened rim notch, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for Volquartsen.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until Volquartsen has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Volquartsen Mamba-TF, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from Volquartsen exists for this model; the pattern source documents a field strip and nothing deeper for an owner. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to Volquartsen, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brush wet with bore solvent, from the chamber end
Dry patches until clean, then a lightly oiled patch for storage
A dry patch through before the next shot

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: A thin film of oil on the bolt’s bearing surfaces
⛔ No oil into the firing-pin channel

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly.title: Safety on, bolt fully into the receiver
reassembly.action: Confirm the pistol is free of cartridges and put the safety on — Ruger requires it for reassembly — then insert the bolt fully into the barrel/receiver assembly.
reassembly.quote: 2. Insert the bolt fully into the barrel/receiver assembly (see Figure 15).

reassembly.title: Notch onto the pivot pin, rotated down until the button clicks
reassembly.action: Set the receiver’s notch over the grip frame’s pivot pin and rotate the barrel/receiver assembly down onto the frame until the take-down button clicks home.
reassembly.quote: 3. Place the barrel/receiver assembly on top of the frame so that the notch in the receiver aligns with the pivot pin in the grip frame (see Figure 16).

fncheck: Magazine out and the chamber proven empty twice. Work the bolt by its ears: it runs freely and returns fully forward. The safety moves between its positions and, when on, locks the works. This check never asks you to pull the trigger — this is a rimfire, and dry firing one is a question only Volquartsen may answer.
